longForm.verdict: ChurchTools gives a UK church a clearly documented European-hosted alternative, with a broad operational feature set and visible package limits. The main decision is whether its people, campus and role limits — plus euro pricing — fit the church’s real operating shape.

decisionLens.heading: Hosting geography is a starting point for due diligence, not the conclusion.
decisionLens.text: German hosting is a meaningful supplier statement for churches assessing data location, but it does not settle the church’s UK data-protection responsibilities. The practical work remains: check the agreement, permissions, processors, retention and exit arrangements.

sections.heading: How the packages scale
sections.question: Which limits will shape the church’s day-to-day use?
paragraphs: ChurchTools publishes packages based on people, campuses, resources and ministry roles. It also lists unlimited groups, calendars, events, check-ins and reports across the packages, alongside a church app and open API.

That makes the shortlist conversation more concrete than a generic feature comparison. Count active people, sites, bookable resources and ministry roles now, then model the next expected growth point and the cost of relevant upgrades.

sections.heading: European hosting and UK responsibility
sections.question: What would the church still need to govern itself?
paragraphs: The supplier says hosted accounts are in Germany and presents this in its GDPR information. That is relevant evidence, but this directory does not treat it as a compliance certification for a UK church.

Ask for the current data-processing terms, sub-processor information, access controls and export route. The church still needs its own lawful basis, retention practice, role design and training for staff and volunteers.

sections.heading: Implementation support and the 30-day test
sections.question: Can the church make a supported decision before migrating?
paragraphs: ChurchTools advertises a 30-day free trial, email support and weekly group video calls with a trainer and other churches. Its pricing page also lists migration as a paid service.

Use the trial to test one people-record workflow, one event or resource booking and one service-planning process. Confirm the scope and cost of migration before committing, especially if historical data or multiple sites matter.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score or a collected user-review sample. It is grounded in the supplier’s pricing, hosting and trial documentation.
themes: Independent user-feedback coverage has not yet been researched for this profile.
The decisive fit questions are package limits, migration scope and the church’s own data governance.
userFeedback.caveat: This is a research gap rather than a judgement on user satisfaction or product quality.

faq.question: Where does ChurchTools say it hosts data?
faq.answer: ChurchTools states that hosted accounts are in Germany. A UK church should still ask for the current contractual, sub-processor and data-protection details.

faq.question: Is there a ChurchTools free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. The supplier advertises a 30-day trial, email support and weekly group video calls during the trial.

faq.question: Does ChurchTools support UK Gift Aid?
faq.answer: Do not infer Gift Aid capability from general giving or finance features. Ask the supplier to demonstrate the declaration, claim and reconciliation workflow required by the church.
